rows.note: Use this for physically dirty things, and also for obscene or dirty language; it is the all-purpose choice for both.

example.english: Your shoes are foul; take them off before coming inside.
example.traditional: 你啲鞋污糟晒，入屋前除咗佢啦。
example.jyutping: nei5 di1 haai4 wu1 zou1 saai3 jap6 uk1 cin4 ceoi4 zo2 keoi5 laa1

rows.note: Choose this when a person, thing, or food is disgusting or loathsome rather than merely physically dirty.

example.english: This dish smells foul; it is too disgusting to eat.
example.traditional: 呢碟餸有陣怪味，真係核突到食唔落。
example.jyutping: ne1 dip6 sung3 jau5 zan6 gwaai3 mei6 zan1 hai6 wat6 dat6 dou3 sik6 m4 lok6

rows.note: Use this in games, tests, or other rule-governed situations when something is against the rules.

example.english: You pushed him just now—that was clearly foul.
example.traditional: 你頭先推人，明明就犯規啦！
example.jyutping: nei5 tau4 sin1 teoi1 jan4 ming4 ming4 zau6 faan6 kwai1 laa1
